problem: The assertion follows the ruling: it checks the maximum deletion-unit duration against batch_ms_max and prints p50 and p95 beside it. It failed in all 3 of my release runs. Run 1 (load 1.78 at start, 6.92 at end, partly my own release build): max 8.236 ms, p50 0.958, p95 0.991, 558 units, 0.667 s. Run 2 (load 6.16): max 9.579 ms, p95 0.989, 542 units, 0.649 s. Run 3 (load 7.38): max 9.685 ms, p95 0.998, 617 units, 0.767 s. Each over-budget unit was off CPU for most of its wall time: 8.24/0.83, 7.96/0.97, 9.58/0.85, 6.17/0.64, 5.92/0.61, 9.69/0.46, 5.51/1.06 and 6.35/0.57 ms (wall/on-CPU). Each run also logged blob unlinks stalled in the kernel: 2, 2 and 7 over 4 ms, up to 9.35 ms. A normal unlink on this volume takes p50 0.044-0.046 ms and p99 0.071-0.085 ms. The unit's own work stays bounded: on-CPU max 1.01-1.14 ms. This matches the profile in ADR draft B-9. The code is not at fault, so under the ruling this is not blocking. Every other WP-B benchmark passed in all 3 runs.
fix: No WP-B change. Orchestrator: run `bash Scripts/verify.sh --perf` on a quiet machine as the reference. If the maximum still fails there and every overrun is a single stalled unlink (the printed 'units over the batch budget' and 'blob unlinks inside the reclaim' lists show this), decide whether batch_ms_max includes the time a blocking executor spends inside one unlink(2). Do not weaken the assertion in WP-B. Optional, doc only: BlobUnits.swift:158 says 'a unit's own work ≤ 1.1 ms on CPU', and one of my runs measured 1.14 ms.

area: tests under TSan (time-limit margin of the larger enumerations)

area: crash-consistency (index commit protocol, step 4; same class as round-3 probe 1 and VP7)
location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Index/IndexCommitUnit.swift:153-166 (replaceCurrent: step 4 renames index.bin over index.prev whenever index.bin exists, valid or not; the step-5 rollback at :164 then moves the invalid file back); interacts with :177-181 (the ENOSPC fallback removes index.tmp unconditionally) and B-28 item 1 ('a rotten ... index.bin names another generation and index.prev is kept')
problem: B-28 says the commit unit never drops the newest valid generation, and its ENOSPC guard is written to protect a rotten index.bin. Step 4 defeats that guard: it moves an invalid index.bin over the only valid generation in index.prev. Timeline from probe VPC2-D, run on unmodified e521940 in a scratch copy. (1) Lifetime 1: q is published, rots and is quarantined (doomed corrupt, durable gen 3), then gen 4 and the durable close gen 5. Disk: bin=5, prev=4. (2) One body byte of index.bin flips. The load rule picks prev (gen 4) and degrades because bin is invalid; committedGeneration=4. (3) Lifetime 2: the launch commit (gen 6) writes and syncs tmp, then step 4 renames rotten bin -> prev, which destroys gen 4. Step 5 (tmp -> bin) fails with EIO, and the rollback moves the rotten file back to bin. Observed: 'after failed launch commit: chosen temporary generation 6'. (4) The volume is full. The next commit hits ENOSPC and removes index.tmp, the only valid generation. currentHolds(4) is false, so it keeps index.prev, which no longer exists. The retry fails. Observed: 'after full volume: chosen nil generation 0 degraded true; files [current]'. (5) Lifetime 3, in both processKill and powerLossKeepMetadata, reports 'no valid index on disk', 'q's record lost', 'lifetime 3 opened degraded' and 'the corrupt-doomed name is served after apply'. This is the same harm as round-3 probe 1 and violates §4.4 and R-STO-4: a corrupt index must never cost the last valid generation. Controls with only two of the three faults (rot+ENOSPC, EIO+ENOSPC) pass, so the loss comes from step 4 overwriting index.prev. It needs a rotten index.bin, EIO on step 5 and ENOSPC in the same process. The pre-B-28 code had the same gap, so this is not a regression from the close-out commits.
fix: In replaceCurrent, move index.bin to index.prev only when index.prev is absent or index.bin holds the committed generation. Otherwise rename the source straight over the invalid index.bin. Pass the unit's `committed` value from both call sites (:100 and :134): `let currentExists = try fileSystem.itemInfo(at: current) != nil; let previousExists = try fileSystem.itemInfo(at: previous) != nil; let moved = currentExists && (!previousExists || IndexCommitUnit.currentHolds(committed, layout: layout, fileSystem: fileSystem))`. I applied exactly this in a scratch copy. VPC2-D then passed ('after full volume: chosen previous generation 4'), and the full suite plus my probes passed ('Test run with 278 tests in 35 suites passed after 6.146 seconds'). Add a StoreRecoveryTests regression test, e.g. 'R-STO-4: a rotten index.bin never replaces a valid index.prev, so EIO on step 5 and then a full volume keep a valid generation'. Lifetime 2 opens over a rotten bin and a valid prev with EIO on the first tmp->bin rename, then runs markSyncDue and close on a full volume. Lifetime 3 must load a valid generation, keep the record and never serve the doomed name. Amend B-28 so step 4 states this condition. The orchestrator must also amend the §4.1 step-4 wording.

area: flaky test (race in the test, production behaviour correct)
problem: The test creates `closing = Task { await harness.store.close() }` and then immediately runs `await bulk.setHolding(false)`. If the closing task has not reached the actor yet, apply C runs plan, writes and commit while the phase is still `.open` and returns normally. The assertion on line 81, which expects `.closed`, then fails. This happened once in my coverage run (load about 10): 'StoreSweepTests.swift:81:15: Expectation failed: an error was expected but none was thrown and "ApplyReport(generation: 4, added: [a], ..., pruned: [b], ...)" was returned'. That made `swift test --enable-code-coverage` exit 1 without merging default.profdata. The production code is correct: after its plan unit, apply calls checkLive() (AssetStore+Apply.swift:136), so C can only commit when close() had not begun. It passed in my other 6 runs (3x plain, TSan, quick, coverage-free).
fix: Before line 79, wait until close #1 is draining: `while await harness.state.core.phase != .closing { await Task.yield() }`. Then release the bulk executor. C's plan unit then resumes into `.closing` and throws `.closed` deterministically, and D is unwound by close.

area: liveness (pending promotion of a vanished index.tmp)
location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Index/IndexCommitUnit.swift:94-108 (promotion branch); Store/AssetStore+Commit.swift:128-131 (pendingPromotion is cleared only on promotedName)
problem: While a promotion is pending, every commit attempt first syncs index.tmp. If index.tmp is gone, the sync throws notFound, pendingPromotion is never cleared, and every later commit in this process fails. That includes the durable flush in close(). Probe VPC2-K: the launch commit's promotion sync fails once (EIO), then index.tmp is removed, and three flushes follow. Observed: 'pending promotion Optional(4); flush errors after index.tmp vanished: [fileSystem(notFound) x3]; still pending Optional(4)'. Not blocking: the store itself never removes index.tmp while the promotion is pending. Reaching this state needs an outside deletion inside the private root, or a rename that reports failure after it took effect (the exclusive rollback then fails too).
fix: In the promotion branch, check `fileSystem.itemInfo(at: index.tmp)` first. If it returns nil (or the sync throws `.notFound`), treat the promotion as done-without-commit: set `outcome.promotedName = true` and leave promotedDurably false, so committedGeneration is not raised. Then continue with steps 1-6. Add a StoreRecoveryTests case.
